en: 125(23.5) *The Sūtra on the Fragrance of Precepts* Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao-san Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
Translated by the Imperial Subject Dharma-bhadra, the Great Master Mingjiao, by Imperial Decree: Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda approached the place where the Buddha was staying; having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I have a slight doubt that I wish to inquire about; I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain it for me.

I observe that there are three kinds of fragrance in the world—namely, root-fragrance, flower-fragrance, and seed-fragrance—and these three kinds of fragrance pervade all places, being smelled whether there is wind or no wind. What kind of fragrance is this?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
"Do not speak thus, saying that these three kinds of fragrance are perceived everywhere when there is wind and also when there is no wind."
These three kinds of incense, whether there is wind or no wind, pervade all places yet cannot be smelled.
Ānanda! If you now wish to hear about the universally pervasive fragrance, you should listen attentively; I shall explain it for you.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I now wish to hear it; I only pray that you will proclaim it.”
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"Regarding the fragrance that pervades the ten directions whether there is wind or no wind: suppose there are laymen or laywomen in the world who uphold the pure precepts of the Buddha and practice various wholesome dharmas—namely, not killing, not stealing, not committing sexual misconduct, not lying, and not drinking intoxicants."
These laymen and laywomen, through the fragrance of such precepts, cause their renown to pervade the ten directions; and all throughout those ten directions praise them, saying:

"In such-and-such a city, there are these laymen and laywomen who uphold the pure precepts of the Buddha and practice various wholesome dharmas—namely, refraining from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and drinking intoxicants."

"By being fully endowed with this dharma of precepts, such a person obtains this fragrance; whether there is wind or no wind, it pervades the ten directions, so that all praise them and they receive love and respect."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
“Of all the flowers and fruits in the world, Even including aloeswood, sandalwood, and musk, Such fragrances as these do not pervade everywhere;
Only the fragrance of the precepts is heard throughout all things.”
Sandalwood, turmeric, and storax, Utpala and mālatī flowers—
Among all such exquisite fragrant blossoms, Only the fragrance of precepts is supreme.
All the worldly incenses such as agallochum and sandalwood have but a faint fragrance that does not spread everywhere;
yet if a person maintains the pure fragrance of the Buddha’s precepts, all the devas will smell it and revere them with love.
Thus fully endowed with pure precepts, and even constantly practicing all wholesome dharmas,
such a person can untie the bonds of the world and remain forever far removed from all māras.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda and the assembly of bhikṣus, having heard the Buddha’s words, received them with joy and faith, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Fragrance of Precepts Spoken by the Buddha.
